text:
The biggest story at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Friday was a player who didn't play. Matvei Michkov was out of the lineup, with teammates finding out only before the game, according to PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor, and Rick Tocchet said afterward Michkov will be back in the lineup on Saturday. Without him, the Flyers beat Vancouver 5-2, and the power play did most of the talking.

Philadelphia went 3 for 5 with the man advantage. Tyson Foerster opened the scoring at 4:55 of the first on a 6% wrist shot, and the Flyers dominated that period, 1.20 expected goals (the quality of chances, added up) to 0.37. Noah Cates, the hero of last week's late win over Montreal, made it 2-0 early in the second, and rookie Porter Martone hammered a power-play slap shot at 10:37 for 3-0.

Then Vancouver woke up. The Canucks won the second period 1.56 to 1.14, Filip Hronek scored at 12:05, and Jake DeBrusk beat Dan Vladar at 2:22 of the third after getting behind the Flyers' third pair. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis called it an "Absolutely filthy finish." At 3-2, the Flyers' win chance had dipped to 77%. Travis Konecny, whose name has come up in trade talk all week, restored the two-goal lead on another power play at 6:02, with Christian Dvorak and Foerster assisting. Sean Couturier finished it into an empty net at 18:40.

Vancouver went 0 for 4 on its own power plays despite 1.03 expected goals from them, and Leevi Meriläinen allowed about a goal more than his 28 shots deserved. Wagner also posted that Filip Chytil got hurt and left the game, another blow for a team already waiting on a specialist's word on Elias Pettersson. Our replays of every shot gave Philadelphia the win 62% of the time, a fair reflection of a game the Flyers mostly controlled. What happens with Michkov from here is the thing everyone in Philadelphia will be watching this weekend. On the ice, at least, his teammates gave the coach a quiet night to talk about.
headline: Flyers' power play buries Canucks on a night Michkov sat
